result.summary:
PASS. Independently re-derived every checkable claim in lib/letflow/design/iss0457-splice-first-wins.md against the real file on main (not copied from the design's own prose or from CODE-DESIGNER's summary).

(1) Section 0 re-verification: read lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex directly. autofix_file/1 at :414-446 confirmed (uses `Jason.decode(raw)` in a `with` at :416, not `Jason.decode!` as the design's prose paraphrases -- a cosmetic prose imprecision only, since decode/decode! share identical duplicate-key resolution and this does not affect any behavioral claim; noted as a MINOR issue below, not gate-failing). splice_top_level_status/2 confirmed at :501-512 (spec at :500). scan_for_status/4 spec+clauses confirmed at :521-540, handle_string_token/5 at :545-567. The false-claim comment text at :487-491 read directly and matches the design's quoted 'Current (false) text' in section 3.1 verbatim, word-for-word. The best-overwrite mechanism at :559-560 read directly: `new_best` is unconditionally constructed and threaded through on every depth-1 'status' match regardless of prior `best` state -- confirmed genuinely last-match-wins by construction, exactly as claimed. Independently re-ran the Jason 1.4.5 duplicate-key probe myself (a fourth/fifth independent measurement, not inherited): `Jason.decode!(~s({"status":"a","status":"b"}))` => `%{"status" => "a"}`, and a second probe `Jason.decode!(~s({"status":"PASS","other":1,"status":"DONE"}))` => `%{"other" => 1, "status" => "PASS"}` -- both confirm FIRST-key-wins on the actual pinned jason (mix.lock line 8: jason 1.4.5), matching the design's claim exactly.

(2) Option (a) is justified in section 1 against the real code (not a historical branch description) with concrete reasoning (Jason's resolution is a fixed point outside this codebase's control; option (b) would require inventing new duplicate-key detection machinery Jason's decode already silently absorbs; zero real occurrences in a 1989-file corpus removes urgency for the heavier option). No .ex function bodies present anywhere in the artefact -- verified by reading the full document: only prose, one unchanged @spec block, and quoted comment/documentation text (the before/after false-claim blocks, which are prose, not code).

(3) Section 2's behavior-change spec is unambiguous: `best` set exactly once, on the first depth-1 'status' match, never overwritten by a later one. The (i)/(ii) implementation choice is explicitly stated as non-load-bearing for observable output, and checked this myself against the real clause shapes (:552-566) -- both converge to an identical final `acc`/`best` regardless of which is chosen, so this is a legitimate implementation-detail fork, not a hidden ambiguity. Every named preserved property traces to real, still-present code: depth-counting clauses (:525-531) untouched by this change; consume_json_string/1 (:610-620) untouched; the depth==1 guard (:548) untouched; splice construction (:504) untouched; the zero-match raise (:506-510) untouched. All citations checked against the actual file, not assumed.

(4) Both corrected-text blocks (section 3.1 for the code comment, section 3.2 for lib/letflow/design/iss0442-lint-handoffs-minimal-diff-autofix.md's own algorithm step 2 at :197-204, read directly and confirmed to match the design's quoted 'Current (false) text' verbatim) state FIRST-key-wins and cite the same jason 1.4.5 probe result I independently reproduced -- factually accurate.

(5) All six Step 2 dispatch acceptance criteria independently checked against the artefact and met: option (a) picked/justified against real main code; behavior-change spec for scan_for_status/4 stated exactly with all named properties addressed; both false-claim locations named with corrected text; zero .ex function-body code (grep for TBD/deferred/'to be determined' also returned no matches); regression-suite impact addressed in section 4 and independently spot-checked -- confirmed test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs has exactly 47 tests (`grep -c '  test '` => 47) and the ISS-0442 comment block at lines ~721-740 (design cites ~722-742, close enough -- same block) matches the design's characterization verbatim: duplicate-top-level-status was investigated and deliberately left uncovered, with no test asserting the old last-wins behavior as correct, and no test fixture in the file constructs a duplicate-key document.

One MINOR issue found and recorded below (does not affect the verdict): section 0's prose says autofix_file/1 decides 'via Map.get(Jason.decode!(raw), "status")' but the real code at :416 uses `Jason.decode(raw)` (non-bang, inside a `with`/`{:ok, data}` match), not `Jason.decode!/1`. This is immaterial to every substantive claim the design makes (decode/1 and decode!/1 apply identical duplicate-key resolution; nothing in sections 1-5 depends on which form is used), so it does not constitute a false claim about behavior and is not gate-failing -- flagged only so the source gets corrected per core-directives.md's 'Never resolve a conflict silently' norm for a MINOR discrepancy.
